closure_differences.expected_direction: less cross-field loss -> higher confinement, higher density / T_e, LARGER cusp potential steps and anode current in our primary run
closure_differences.ours: NONE in the primary run (accepted v1.3 closure); the sealed variant 'bohm-0.4' switches the v1.4 isotropic Bohm-scattering hook on at alpha = 0.4 (nu_an = alpha omega_ce -> D_perp ~ alpha k T_e / e B for alpha << 1; at 0.4 the exact factor is alpha / (1 + alpha^2) = 0.345) - a DIFFERENT model of the same coefficient (isotropic redirect changes the parallel speed too)
closure_differences.reference: Bohm-type D_perp = 0.4 k T_e / (e B) by perpendicular-velocity rotation

closure_differences.expected_direction: our dielectric floats more negative -> larger sheath drop, fewer wall electron losses
closure_differences.reference: 50 % of impacting electrons re-emitted at 90 % of the incident energy

closure_differences.expected_direction: our ionisation is redistributed toward the exit relative to the reference (their n_g is 3x higher near the anode)
closure_differences.reference: static DSMC profile ~6e20 -> ~1e20 along the channel (mean ~2e20), 500 K, diffuse walls

closure_differences.expected_direction: our anode current is conditioned on the reference's outcome by construction: I_a - I_inj (= the ionisation-borne current) is the independent part
closure_differences.ours: channel-only: 1.8 mA at 1 eV injected at the exit plane (the reference's continuity-derived effective source, TAKEN FROM ITS RESULTS: I_anode - I_beam)
closure_differences.reference: uniform 1 eV volume source of 17.55 mA on the outer rim of a 6.48 mm plume box, of which ~1.8-1.95 mA reach the channel

closure_differences.expected_direction: the whole 400 V drop is forced inside our channel: the exit cell potential, the ion exit energy and everything downstream are not comparable (comparable_under)
closure_differences.ours: Dirichlet 0 V exit plane at 14 mm (channel-only)
closure_differences.reference: plume box to 20.48 mm with 0 V far boundaries; the main potential drop forms a 'bulge' beyond the exit

closure_differences.expected_direction: the reference's cusp potential dips and sheath structure are those of a relatively larger-Debye plasma; our dips may be sharper
closure_differences.reference: factor 4 (paper) / 8 (thesis): lambda_D / L larger by 2.0 / 2.83 in the reference plasma; sheaths relatively thicker

closure_differences.expected_direction: second-order for the channel scalars; CEX matters for the plume
closure_differences.ours: e-n elastic / one lumped excitation / single ionisation (Biagi v7.1); no Coulomb, no CEX, no Xe2+
closure_differences.reference: e-n elastic / excitation / ionisation (LLNL EEDL), Coulomb, CEX, Xe2+ (thesis)

closure_differences.expected_direction: steady-state wall potential is set by the plasma either way; the transient charging and the non-local coupling differ
closure_differences.ours: surface charge on a perfect-insulator backing (no field inside the dielectric)
closure_differences.reference: 1 mm Al2O3 (epsilon_r 9) between the plasma and the grounded body, surface charge included

closure_differences.expected_direction: with static neutrals no slow variable remains; a plateau in a few transits is plausible but the reference's 76 us is the longer average
closure_differences.ours: plateau rule: >= 3 transits (4.2 us) with trailing-20 % drifts < 5 % of I_d and N_e
closure_differences.reference: 76 us from a seeded plasma column, averaged over 3.2 us
